conclusions.detail: If a metric was computed ad hoc, it does not exist. Notes and conclusions hold the qualitative read and LINK to runs.

conclusions.statement: The SME lock is absolute, and supersession is explicit.
conclusions.detail: A machine never overwrites an adjudicated row; a newer human ruling supersedes an older one via the gold merge, and every superseded row goes to the reviewer as a confirmation list, never silently.

conclusions.statement: Canonical forms come from adjudicated sources, not batch frequency.
conclusions.detail: Three Korean rules over-fired before this was learned; one 'repaired' 13 rows away from the reviewer's own approved answer.

conclusions.statement: Repair by minimal substitution; re-translate only for structure.
conclusions.detail: Free re-translation takes the licence it is given — it once cleared a rule while deleting 'emission' from a SPECT term. A substitution touches exactly the offending span.
The Korean priority-validation result is credible because the sample was stratified and blinded and the analysis was written down before the reviewer saw the file.

conclusions.statement: Expect the reviewer to supersede herself.
conclusions.detail: Rulings evolve (plain X-ray reversed between rounds; hip went three ways in one file). Confirmation lists and adjudication questions metabolise this.

conclusions.statement: Pair-level detectors catch what row-level checks cannot.
conclusions.detail: Duplicate-translation found wrong-vessel and wrong-organ errors every other detector passed — in both generations of the Korean text.

conclusions.statement: Single-run A/Bs at production temperature are not decision evidence.
conclusions.detail: Sampling noise flips ~7-8% of rows between identical runs; per-row causal traces (retained prompts) are the usable evidence at small scale.

conclusions.statement: Derived data is never edited in place.
conclusions.detail: Pools, gold sets, and deliverables version through tracked runs with content digests, so rollback is always one flow away.
